question: In the context of the ongoing dispute over Russian oil transit through Ukraine and the threat of Hungary and Slovakia halting emergency electricity supplies, Ukrainian veteran Yevhen Dykyi, former commander of the Aidar battalion, has spoken out.

In an interview with Ukrainian media, he suggested that Ukraine could use force to enter Slovak and Hungarian territory and take over infrastructure if supplies are stopped1. Dykyi, now a respected commentator and army advisor, likened this to Trumpian ‘language of force’ and spoke derisively of the strength of the Hungarian and Slovak armed forces.

This outburst is causing tension in Ukraine’s relations with the EU, particularly in light of the fact that the Union is supporting Ukraine with weapons and billions of euros. This is a worrying sign that the trust between these partners is waning. 1.
How does the Commission plan to respond to these threats of military intervention against EU Member States from such an influential Ukrainian voice?
What will the EU do to ensure that such statements do not undermine confidence in cooperation with Ukraine and threaten the security of its Member States?
Does the EU intend to take diplomatic steps aimed at urging the Ukrainian Government to condemn these statements and prevent further escalation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.4.2026) The EU remains committed to supporting Ukraine in the face of Russia’s ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine, while also maintaining close cooperation and trust with all Member States.

In this context, it is important to distinguish clearly between official positions of the Ukrainian government and statements made by individual commentators or former military personnel. The Commission underlines that any suggestion of the use of force against the territorial integrity of Member States is incompatible with the principles of the UN Charter.

The EU has seen no indication that the Government of Ukraine supports such views. On the contrary, the EU’s partnership with Ukraine is based on shared commitments to international law and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. The EU remains attentive to developments in the regional energy situation caused by Russia’s attacks on civilian infrastructure.

The EU’s response has been further intensified, including efforts to enhance the resilience and recovery of Ukraine’s energy system. In addition to largescale infrastructure support, the EU is focusing on assisting the most vulnerable regions and cities.

Part of the 2026 winter support package under the Ukraine Facility will be implemented through the Ukraine Energy Support Fund and will focus on the physical protection of energy infrastructure as well as urgent repairs.
